newsitem.title: LATVIA: EXPORTS RISE FASTER THAN IMPORTS IN H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: EXPORTS RISE FASTER THAN IMPORTS IN H1 1997.

text.p: Latvian exports in the first six
months of 1997 rose by 23.1 percent compared to the same period
last year to 454.9 million lats, the country's statistics
committee said on Friday.
The committee also said in a statement that imports rose to
713.2 million lats in the first half of 1997, an increase of
22.2 percent compared to the same period last year.
The committee said that the European Union was the
country's leading importer at 53.1 percent compared to 49.5
percent in the same period last year, followed by the CIS at
19.9 percent compared to 25.5 percent in the first half of
The EU also accounted for 50.8 percent of all of the
country's exports compared to 42.8 percent last year. Of total
exports, 28.2 percent went to the CIS in the first half of 1997
versus 38.5 percent in the same period last year.
Wood products accounted for 31.7 percent of all exports in
the first six months of 1996 followed by textiles at 16.2
percent.
Cars, electrical parts and mechanical equipment accounted
for 19.2 percent of all imports followed by mineral products at
14.2 percent.
